8: use clap::builder::ValueParser;
9: use clap::parser::ValuesRef;
10: use clap::{crate_version, Arg, ArgAction, ArgMatches, Command};
11: use std::ffi::OsString;
12: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
13: #[cfg(not(windows))]
14: use uucore::error::FromIo;
15: use uucore::error::{UResult, USimpleError};
16: #[cfg(not(windows))]
17: use uucore::mode;
18: use uucore::{display::Quotable, fs::dir_strip_dot_for_creation};
19: use uucore::{format_usage, help_about, help_section, help_usage, show_if_err};
20: 
21: static DEFAULT_PERM: u32 = 0o777;
22: 
23: const ABOUT: &str = help_about!("mkdir.md");
24: const USAGE: &str = help_usage!("mkdir.md");
25: const AFTER_HELP: &str = help_section!("after help", "mkdir.md");
26: 
27: mod options {
28:     pub const MODE: &str = "mode";
29:     pub const PARENTS: &str = "parents";
30:     pub const VERBOSE: &str = "verbose";
31:     pub const DIRS: &str = "dirs";
32: }
33: 
34: #[cfg(windows)]
35: fn get_mode(_matches: &ArgMatches, _mode_had_minus_prefix: bool) -> Result<u32, String> {
36:     Ok(DEFAULT_PERM)
37: }
38: 
39: #[cfg(not(windows))]
40: fn get_mode(matches: &ArgMatches, mode_had_minus_prefix: bool) -> Result<u32, String> {
41:     // Not tested on Windows
42:     let mut new_mode = DEFAULT_PERM;
43: 
44:     if let Some(m) = matches.get_one::<String>(options::MODE) {
45:         for mode in m.split(',') {
46:             if mode.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
47:                 new_mode = mode::parse_numeric(new_mode, m, true)?;
48:             } else {
49:                 let cmode = if mode_had_minus_prefix {
50:                     // clap parsing is finished, now put prefix back
51:                     format!("-{mode}")
52:                 } else {
53:                     mode.to_string()
54:                 };
55:                 new_mode = mode::parse_symbolic(new_mode, &cmode, mode::get_umask(), true)?;
56:             }
57:         }
58:         Ok(new_mode)
59:     } else {
60:         // If no mode argument is specified return the mode derived from umask
61:         Ok(!mode::get_umask() & 0o0777)
62:     }
63: }
64: 
65: #[cfg(windows)]
66: fn strip_minus_from_mode(_args: &mut [String]) -> bool {
67:     false
68: }
69: 
70: #[cfg(not(windows))]
71: fn strip_minus_from_mode(args: &mut Vec<String>) -> bool {
72:     mode::strip_minus_from_mode(args)
73: }
74: 
75: #[uucore::main]
76: pub fn uumain(args: impl uucore::Args) -> UResult<()> {
77:     let mut args = args.collect_lossy();
78: 
79:     // Before we can parse 'args' with clap (and previously getopts),
80:     // a possible MODE prefix '-' needs to be removed (e.g. "chmod -x FILE").
81:     let mode_had_minus_prefix = strip_minus_from_mode(&mut args);
82: 
83:     // Linux-specific options, not implemented
84:     // opts.optflag("Z", "context", "set SELinux security context" +
85:     // " of each created directory to CTX"),
86:     let matches = uu_app().after_help(AFTER_HELP).try_get_matches_from(args)?;
87: 
88:     let dirs = matches
89:         .get_many::<OsString>(options::DIRS)
90:         .unwrap_or_default();
91:     let verbose = matches.get_flag(options::VERBOSE);
92:     let recursive = matches.get_flag(options::PARENTS);
93: 
94:     match get_mode(&matches, mode_had_minus_prefix) {
95:         Ok(mode) => exec(dirs, recursive, mode, verbose),
96:         Err(f) => Err(USimpleError::new(1, f)),
97:     }
98: }

100: pub fn uu_app() -> Command {
101:     Command::new(uucore::util_name())
102:         .version(crate_version!())
103:         .about(ABOUT)
104:         .override_usage(format_usage(USAGE))
105:         .infer_long_args(true)
106:         .arg(
107:             Arg::new(options::MODE)
108:                 .short('m')
109:                 .long(options::MODE)
110:                 .help("set file mode (not implemented on windows)"),
111:         )
112:         .arg(
113:             Arg::new(options::PARENTS)
114:                 .short('p')
115:                 .long(options::PARENTS)
116:                 .help("make parent directories as needed")
117:                 .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
118:         )
119:         .arg(
120:             Arg::new(options::VERBOSE)
121:                 .short('v')
122:                 .long(options::VERBOSE)
123:                 .help("print a message for each printed directory")
124:                 .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
125:         )
126:         .arg(
127:             Arg::new(options::DIRS)
128:                 .action(ArgAction::Append)
129:                 .num_args(1..)
130:                 .value_parser(ValueParser::os_string())
131:                 .value_hint(clap::ValueHint::DirPath),
132:         )
133: }

135: /**
136:  * Create the list of new directories
137:  */
138: fn exec(dirs: ValuesRef<OsString>, recursive: bool, mode: u32, verbose: bool) -> UResult<()> {
139:     for dir in dirs {
140:         let path_buf = PathBuf::from(dir);
141:         let path = path_buf.as_path();
142: 
143:         show_if_err!(mkdir(path, recursive, mode, verbose));
144:     }
145:     Ok(())
146: }
147: 
148: /// Create directory at a given `path`.
149: ///
150: /// ## Options
151: ///
152: /// * `recursive` --- create parent directories for the `path`, if they do not
153: ///     exist.
154: /// * `mode` --- file mode for the directories (not implemented on windows).
155: /// * `verbose` --- print a message for each printed directory.
156: ///
157: /// ## Trailing dot
158: ///
159: /// To match the GNU behavior, a path with the last directory being a single dot
160: /// (like `some/path/to/.`) is created (with the dot stripped).
161: pub fn mkdir(path: &Path, recursive: bool, mode: u32, verbose: bool) -> UResult<()> {
162:     // Special case to match GNU's behavior:
163:     // mkdir -p foo/. should work and just create foo/
164:     // std::fs::create_dir("foo/."); fails in pure Rust
165:     let path_buf = dir_strip_dot_for_creation(path);
166:     let path = path_buf.as_path();
167: 
168:     create_dir(path, recursive, verbose, false)?;
169:     chmod(path, mode)
170: }
171: 
172: #[cfg(any(unix, target_os = "redox"))]
173: fn chmod(path: &Path, mode: u32) -> UResult<()> {
174:     use std::fs::{set_permissions, Permissions};
175:     use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
176: 
177:     let mode = Permissions::from_mode(mode);
178: 
179:     set_permissions(path, mode)
180:         .map_err_context(|| format!("cannot set permissions {}", path.quote()))
181: }
182: 
183: #[cfg(windows)]
184: fn chmod(_path: &Path, _mode: u32) -> UResult<()> {
185:     // chmod on Windows only sets the readonly flag, which isn't even honored on directories
186:     Ok(())
187: }
188: 
189: // `is_parent` argument is not used on windows
190: #[allow(unused_variables)]
191: fn create_dir(path: &Path, recursive: bool, verbose: bool, is_parent: bool) -> UResult<()> {
192:     if path.exists() && !recursive {
193:         return Err(USimpleError::new(
194:             1,
195:             format!("{}: File exists", path.display()),
196:         ));
197:     }
198:     if path == Path::new("") {
199:         return Ok(());
200:     }
201: 
202:     if recursive {
203:         match path.parent() {
204:             Some(p) => create_dir(p, recursive, verbose, true)?,
205:             None => {
206:                 USimpleError::new(1, "failed to create whole tree");
207:             }
208:         }
209:     }
210:     match std::fs::create_dir(path) {
211:         Ok(()) => {
212:             if verbose {
213:                 println!(
214:                     "{}: created directory {}",
215:                     uucore::util_name(),
216:                     path.quote()
217:                 );
218:             }
219:             #[cfg(not(windows))]
220:             if is_parent {
221:                 // directories created by -p have permission bits set to '=rwx,u+wx',
222:                 // which is umask modified by 'u+wx'
223:                 chmod(path, (!mode::get_umask() & 0o0777) | 0o0300)?;
224:             }
225:             Ok(())
226:         }
227:         Err(_) if path.is_dir() => Ok(()),
228:         Err(e) => Err(e.into()),
229:     }
230: }

part.text:
Implemented the fix in `src/uu/mkdir/src/mkdir.rs`.

`create_dir` now reports whether it actually created the directory, and `mkdir` only applies `chmod` when a new directory was created. Existing directories passed with `-p` are left untouched, so `mkdir -p /root` as a non-root user no longer fails.

Validation:
- All 18 `mkdir` tests pass, including the previously failing existing-last-component permission test.
- Reproduced `mkdir -p /root` as `nobody`: exits `0`.
